story: Gov.-elect Kreiss-Tomkins asks the AIDEA board to pause until he takes office December 7th; the board meets in closed session, takes no action, resumes Tuesday and meets again December 4th

source_fetch_summary.notes: Five targeted repeats where the first response was a summary; two AIDEA PDFs read locally; Beacon via feed (article 403); KTOO republication guess 404.

claims.claim: Gov.-elect Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins asked the AIDEA board to postpone further action until after the new administration takes office.
claims.verbatim: postpone further action until after the new administration has taken office.
claims.notes: Must Read Alaska quotes the same words from his statement. Press release itself not fetched.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins takes office on December 7th.
claims.verbatim: as he prepares to take office on Dec. 7.
claims.notes: Also ADN Nov 19, Beacon, Mat-Su Sentinel.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins made the request one hour before the AIDEA board's scheduled Thursday meeting.
claims.verbatim: One hour before a scheduled board meeting of the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority on Thursday

claims.claim: According to the Alaska Beacon, Kreiss-Tomkins's statement says AIDEA's board has made $200 million in financial commitments since October.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA’s board has made $200 million in financial commitments since October
claims.notes: Governor-elect's figure as Beacon reports it. CONFLICT with Must Read Alaska's reading (C08, C09). Attribute.

claims.claim: According to the Alaska Beacon, Kreiss-Tomkins's statement says the board could make $150 million more in commitments on short notice.
claims.verbatim: has the potential to make $150 million more on short notice.
claims.notes: CONFLICT with C09. Do not sum with C04. Attribute and hedge.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins described the board's pace as an extraordinary rush to approve potentially irreversible spending.
claims.verbatim: concerned about this extraordinary rush to approve potentially irreversible spending
claims.notes: Beacon attributes these words to his written statement.

claims.claim: The Beacon reported the request came with fewer than three weeks left in the current administration.
claims.verbatim: with fewer than three weeks left in Alaska’s current administration,
claims.notes: Not confirmed as his quoted wording. November 19th to December 7th is 18 days.

claims.claim: Must Read Alaska reported that the board met on November 19th to consider changes to a proposed expenditure of more than $200,000,000 in public funds.
claims.verbatim: proposed expenditure of more than $200,000,000 in public funds

claims.claim: Must Read Alaska reported that since October 21st the board authorized more than an additional $150,000,000 in public funds.
claims.verbatim: authorization to spend more than an additional $150,000,000 in public funds

claims.claim: The Kreiss-Tomkins statement said the board was acting despite a lack of transparent due diligence and public review.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA’s board is voting to take these actions despite a lack of transparent due diligence and public review
claims.notes: Paraphrase with attribution; quotation marks not confirmed.

claims.claim: The November 19th meeting was the AIDEA board's third since the election.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA’s Thursday board meeting was its third since the election.
claims.notes: Reconciles with C12/C24: Oct 21, Nov 4, Nov 6 (continuation), Nov 19.

claims.claim: Must Read Alaska reported the November 19th meeting was the fourth time the board had met since October 21st.
claims.verbatim: This marks the fourth time the board has met since October 21.
claims.notes: Matches the primary schedule if Nov 6 continuation counts.

claims.claim: Becky Windt Pearson said AIDEA had held four board meetings with a fifth scheduled for the first week of December.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA has had four different board meetings, and a fifth is scheduled for the first week of December

claims.claim: The AIDEA board met in a closed-door executive session that began at 10 a.m. on November 19th.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA’s board was in the fourth hour of a closed-door executive session that began at 10 a.m.

claims.claim: At 3 p.m. the AIDEA board adjourned for the day without taking action.
claims.verbatim: At 3 p.m., the board adjourned for the day without taking action.

claims.claim: The AIDEA board was scheduled to resume meeting on Tuesday.
claims.verbatim: They are scheduled to resume meeting on Tuesday.
claims.notes: November 24th is a calculation; no page prints it.

claims.claim: At its Tuesday meeting the board could vote on a $175 million expenditure on oil exploration in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.
claims.verbatim: including on a $175 million expenditure on oil exploration in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.

claims.claim: The board is scheduled to meet again on December 4th, three days before Kreiss-Tomkins takes office.
claims.verbatim: The board is scheduled to meet again Dec. 4, three days before Kreiss-Tomkins takes office.

claims.claim: AIDEA's agenda lists its next regular board meeting for Friday December 4th at the Alaska Housing Finance Corporation Board Room in Anchorage.
claims.verbatim: Next regularly scheduled AIDEA Board Meeting: Friday, December 4, 2026. This meeting will be held in the Alaska Housing Finance Corporation Board Room, 4300 Boniface Parkway,
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority

claims.claim: AIDEA's November 19th board meeting was held by teleconference starting at 10 a.m.
claims.verbatim: Board Meeting via teleconference, Thursday, November 19, 2026 at 10:00:00 a.m.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority

claims.claim: The November 19th agenda set an executive session on ANWR, Ambler, real estate, AIDEA owned assets and AIDEA finances.
claims.verbatim: Executive Session: Confidential and deliberative matters related to: ANWR, Ambler, Real Estate, AIDEA Owned Assets, and AIDEA Finances.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: Grounds cited: deliberative process and attorney-client privilege.

claims.claim: The November 19th agenda included a review of Resolution G26-05, the Section 1002 Area Development Budget.
claims.verbatim: Review and Status of Resolution G26-05 Section 1002 Area Development Budget
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: Section 1002 Area is the ANWR coastal plain.

claims.claim: The November 19th agenda included an amended second resolution G26-07 on Port Mackenzie infrastructure and real estate.
claims.verbatim: Amended Second Resolution G26-07 Port Mackenzie Infrastructure and Real Estate
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority

claims.claim: AIDEA's schedule lists its November 6th session as a continuation of the November 4th board meeting.
claims.verbatim: Continued November 4, 2026, Board Meeting
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: Schedule also lists Oct 21 (G26-11, G26-12), Nov 4 (G26-13 to G26-15), Nov 6 (amended G25-07), Nov 19, Dec 4.

claims.claim: AIDEA executive director Randy Ruaro said Alaskans can be proud of AIDEA.
claims.verbatim: Alaskans can be proud of AIDEA.
claims.notes: Ruaro signaled no pause per ADN (paraphrase only).

claims.claim: Ruaro told the board AIDEA had accomplished record revenue three years in a row.
claims.verbatim: We’ve accomplished record revenue three years in a row.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins named Becky Windt Pearson senior transition adviser on AIDEA.
claims.verbatim: Windt Pearson will serve as senior transition adviser on AIDEA

claims.claim: The transition team said Windt Pearson would lead the review of AIDEA's operations, governance and strategic direction.
claims.verbatim: a leading role in the incoming administration's review of (AIDEA's) operations, governance, and strategic direction.

claims.claim: Windt Pearson ended a four-month stint with LNG developer Glenfarne to take the AIDEA role.
claims.verbatim: To take the job, Windt Pearson ends a four-month stint with Glenfarne

claims.claim: Windt Pearson said the transition team is concerned and focused on the high amount of activity in the closing days of the administration.
claims.verbatim: concerned and focused on the high amount of activity that’s happening here at the very closing days of the administration.
claims.notes: Retrieved from the November 19th ADN article.

claims.claim: AIDEA Resolution G26-11 authorized creating NorthStar Fiber Development LLC as a wholly owned subsidiary.
claims.verbatim: AUTHORIZING THE CREATION OF NORTHSTAR FIBER DEVELOPMENT LLC OR AN EQUIVALENT LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY AS A WHOLLY OWNED SUBSIDIARY OF THE AUTHORITY
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: Background document used for a current claim.

claims.claim: Resolution G26-11 capped the fiber subsidiary's capitalization at $75,000,000.
claims.verbatim: APPROVING THE CAPITALIZATION OF THE SUBSIDIARY IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $75,000,000
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: KTOO says authorized, not yet committed.

claims.claim: Resolution G26-11 was dated October 21st.
claims.verbatim: DATED at Anchorage, Alaska, this 21st day of October 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority

claims.claim: AIDEA committed $25 million to NuCube Energy, an Idaho startup designing small nuclear reactors.
claims.verbatim: a $25 million investment in NuCube Energy, an Idaho-based startup that’s designing small nuclear reactors

claims.claim: AIDEA approved up to $10 million for an equity stake in GeoAlaska.
claims.verbatim: up to $10 million for a second equity deal, this one to acquire a stake in GeoAlaska
claims.notes: Page's own dash replaced by a comma in this field. Single source.

claims.claim: KTOO reported an estimated $86 million in AIDEA spending on preliminary Ambler Road work.
claims.verbatim: an estimated $86 million in spending on preliminary work on the proposed Ambler Road

claims.claim: AIDEA greenlit more than $50 million in cash and loans for shipyard projects in Wrangell and Ketchikan.
claims.verbatim: more than $50 million in cash and loans for shipyard projects

claims.claim: KTOO reported that AIDEA spending announcements totaled more than $200 million since August.
claims.verbatim: The spending announcements have totaled more than $200 million since August
claims.notes: Reporter's tally; different window from C04.

claims.claim: AIDEA allocated $20 million for Alaska Data Corp earlier this year.
claims.verbatim: allocated $20 million for Alaska Data Corp. earlier this year.

claims.claim: On November 9th AIDEA launched an investment platform run by a new subsidiary.
claims.verbatim: on Nov. 9, AIDEA launched an investment platform run by a new subsidiary

claims.claim: AIDEA generated more than $60 million in net income in each of the past three years.
claims.verbatim: generated more than $60 million in net income each of the past three years

claims.claim: AIDEA paid $52 million in total dividends to the state over the past three years.
claims.verbatim: $52 million in total dividends for the state government over that period.

claims.claim: Last year AIDEA paid the state a dividend of roughly $15.5 million.
claims.verbatim: Last year, it paid the state a dividend of roughly $15.5 million.

claims.claim: ADN reported AIDEA created a subsidiary to advance data centers despite a campaign promise from Kreiss-Tomkins.
claims.verbatim: despite a campaign promise from Kreiss-Tomkins
claims.notes: Substance of the promise not verbatim; do not state pause or moratorium in his words.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins has said he would completely reassess AIDEA.
claims.verbatim: Kreiss-Tomkins said he would “completely reassess” AIDEA if elected

claims.claim: Gov. Mike Dunleavy responded that the people of Alaska elected him for a full term.
claims.verbatim: the people of Alaska elected me for a full term and expect their governor to keep working on behalf of the people

claims.claim: The Beacon reported that AIDEA has sought a large tract of land near Houston for industrial development.
claims.verbatim: It also has sought a large tract of land near Houston for industrial development

claims.claim: The state approved transferring about 6,800 acres of land near Houston to AIDEA.
claims.verbatim: transfer about 6,800 acres of land near Houston to the state's development corporation.
claims.source_outlet: Mat-Su Sentinel via Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: The Mat-Su Borough letter asking DNR to reconsider was signed by Borough Manager Mike Brown and Mayor Edna DeVries.
claims.verbatim: The letter is signed by Borough Manager Mike Brown and Mayor Edna DeVries.
claims.source_outlet: Mat-Su Sentinel via Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: The borough letter says the projects should instead be built near Point MacKenzie and in the West Susitna area.
claims.verbatim: Those projects should instead be built near Point MacKenzie and in the West Susitna area, it states.
claims.source_outlet: Mat-Su Sentinel via Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: DNR received more than 2,300 public comments on the no-cost transfer.
claims.verbatim: more than 2,300 public comments regarding the no-cost transfer.
claims.source_outlet: Mat-Su Sentinel via Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: About $180 million has been spent on a Point MacKenzie rail bed slated for about $249 million in new federal completion funding.
claims.verbatim: $180 million spent on a rail bed that is slated to receive about $249 million in new federal funding for completion.
claims.source_outlet: Mat-Su Sentinel via Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: Anyone who commented during the proposal process can request reconsideration by November 30th.
claims.verbatim: Anyone who submitted a comment during the proposal process can request reconsideration by Nov. 30.
claims.source_outlet: Mat-Su Sentinel via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: DNR has 30 days to address requests.

claims.claim: The Houston land transfer is the subject of a pending lawsuit.
claims.verbatim: The transfer is also the subject of a pending lawsuit.
claims.source_outlet: Mat-Su Sentinel via Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission approved Mayor Grier Hopkins's proposed moratorium on permits for large-scale data centers.
claims.verbatim: approved Mayor Grier Hopkins’ proposed moratorium on permits for large-scale data centers,

claims.claim: The Planning Commission extended the proposed moratorium from 12 months to 18 months.
claims.verbatim: extending the mayor’s proposed 12-month timeframe to 18.

claims.claim: The commission lengthened the administration's research deadline from six months to 10.
claims.verbatim: from six months to 10.

claims.claim: Hopkins said the Assembly vote will likely take place on January 14th.
claims.verbatim: with Hopkins saying a vote will likely take place on Jan. 14.

claims.claim: Hopkins said the borough is trying to turn the gray area over data centers near Eielson Air Force Base black and white.
claims.verbatim: trying to figure out how to turn that gray area black and white.

claims.claim: KTOO reported AIDEA authorized up to $75 million for a new state-owned company promoting broadband.
claims.verbatim: up to $75 million for a new state-owned company promoting broadband.
claims.notes: Quoted by the fact-checker from the KTOO fetch as corroboration of C32; KTOO says authorized, not yet committed.

killed.claim: Ruaro hopes for additional positive announcements soon
Ruaro: not rapidly moving through projects without due diligence
Windt Pearson: job is not to stop or approve particular projects
Kreiss-Tomkins promised a data center pause or moratorium
killed.why: substance not verbatim in window; only 'despite a campaign promise' (C44)

killed.claim: The November 9th platform is named InvestNorth

killed.why: sources conflict on past vs future

killed.claim: AIDEA paid about $15 million this year
killed.why: summary only; ADN's $15.5 million last year kept

killed.claim: Hopkins open houses, GVEA and North Pole Water
Spokesperson declined Nov 10 on Houston reversal
G26-13 to G26-15 contents; Alaska Data Corp tied to January 21st
